Two rotations with the `steady` history that take their grid from `#Global`: the global `set` row dated 2026-06-01 carries `period=1w, anchor, horizon=6w, tolerance=7`; the bare `anchor` is needed because a global `period` never anchors by itself (DESIGN 3.5). `primary`'s first row is an empty `set` row, the minimal first row of a rotation whose settings all come from `#Global`; `secondary`'s first row is `set tolerance=0`, overriding that one key. Neither pins an anchor locally, so a later global period change would re-anchor both (a bare `anchor` in a rotation would pin it there instead). Both rotations give alice 20 extra points with a `score` row at the 09-07 snapshot, which the snapshot records since state rows dated at `S` apply before it (3.6), so she stands at 48 against 28, 28, 21 and 21 and is out of the band in both rotations for the whole six-week horizon, which is why the generated shifts match `steady`'s shape; the point of the fixture is the settings. The `#Status` settings blocks show the source of every key: in `primary` `period`, `anchor`, `horizon` and `tolerance` come from `global`; in `secondary` `tolerance` comes from the `rotation`. `#Global` is written back with its comment and set row unchanged, and the `tabs` block counts one `#Global` row (comments do not count).
